claims.shortExcerpt: Scientific Name: Theobroma cacao subsp. cacao… / known as Theobroma cacao.
Common Names: cocoa and chocolate (English), cacao (Spanish), cacaoyer and cacaotier (French), kakao (German), cacau (Portuguese).
plants may be damaged or killed during prolonged cool or brief freezing temperatures. / very fragile to both frost and wind gusts.
Temperatures below 50°F (10°C) may damage or kill the plant… South Florida’s warm subtropical environment is very marginal for cocoa growing.
Optimum temperatures for cocoa growth range from 65 to 90°F (18–32°C). Temperatures in excess of 90°F (32°C) may limit plant growth.
adapted to and grow best in hot, humid tropical areas… / Humidity levels of 80% are considered to be ideal for growing it.
Cocoa require access to soil moisture (water) nearly year round… Drought stress leads to leaf and flower drop and poor fruit production.

Cocoa plants require well drained soil… / needs well-draining soil as it does not do well in flooded conditions.

Cocoa plants are adapted to and grow best in hot, humid tropical areas… striking pods (fruit).

claims.value: Cauliflorous flowering on older wood; flowering only when temperatures are at or above 68°F (20°C). Drought stress causes flower drop.
claims.shortExcerpt: Flowering only occurs when temperatures are at or above 68°F(20°C). … Drought stress leads to leaf and flower drop…

claims.value: Produces pods (drupes); flower to mature pod typically 5–7 months. Needs near year-round soil moisture; drought causes poor fruit production. Pollination may require compatible varieties or hand pollination where midges are absent.
claims.shortExcerpt: time from flower pollination to a fully developed pod takes 5 to 7 months or more. … Drought stress leads to … poor fruit production.

claims.value: Reliable outdoor survival and productivity need hot, humid, frost-free tropical conditions with steady moisture. Warm subtropical sites can be marginal; brief freezes or prolonged cool periods may damage or kill plants. Frost-free alone is not sufficient without humidity/moisture fit.
claims.shortExcerpt: South Florida’s warm subtropical environment is very marginal for cocoa growing, and plants may be damaged or killed during prolonged cool or brief freezing temperatures.

claims.value: Hot humid tropical; high frost sensitivity
claims.shortExcerpt: evolved as an understory shade tree in hot, humid, tropical rainforest areas… with well distributed rainfall.

claims.value: Partial shade (~25% shade); filtered light; avoid deep shade for productivity
claims.shortExcerpt: Cocoa is a shade plant and grows best with about 25% shade. … cocoa planted in deep shade tends to be spindly and non-productive.

claims.value: High; keep soil moisture nearly year-round with good drainage; avoid drought and waterlogging
claims.shortExcerpt: Cocoa require access to soil moisture (water) nearly year round… Plants growing in sandy or rocky soils … should be watered every other day or every day during hot, dry conditions.

claims.value: Small to medium tropical understory tree
claims.shortExcerpt: Cocoa are small to medium sized trees (25–30 ft; 7.6–9.1 m) with few branches under tropical environments.

claims.value: About 7.6–9.1 m in tropical conditions; often kept lower (6–8 ft) in home landscapes
claims.shortExcerpt: Cocoa are small to medium sized trees (25–30 ft; 7.6–9.1 m)… Plant height should be limited to 6 to 8 ft…

claims.value: Understory tropical tree needing heat, high humidity, frost-free conditions, partial shade, wind protection, and steady soil moisture with drainage. Sensitive to freezes and prolonged cool weather.
claims.shortExcerpt: Cocoa does not tolerate windy conditions… Temperatures below 50°F (10°C) may damage or kill the plant.
